pebDhu6rItM.desc: Chapter 5 begins here!  This video focuses the varied contributions of Willhelm Wundt, and why we think of him as the father of psychology.

Hb01ht88Xuk.title: Module 4B - Ebbinghaus & Calkins
Hb01ht88Xuk.desc: Continuing on with Chapter 5, this lecture highlights the contributions of Hermann Von Ebbinghaus and Mary Whiton Calkins

TKJ_m_caZYM.title: Module 4C - Brentano and the Würzburg School
TKJ_m_caZYM.desc: This video covers the last part of Chapter 5, kind of coming full circle on some of Wundt's ideas by highlighting how the Würzburg school took them a different direction.

d3eB7vLj254.title: Module 4D - King James
d3eB7vLj254.desc: Of course I mean the King James of Psychology, not that annoying basketball player that beat out the Raptors.  We're talking William James in both this and the next video, both covering Chapter 6 of our course.

LwV1pI2ffWU.title: Module 4E - King James II

RcmlC7KLN38.title: Module 5A - Sigmund Freud
RcmlC7KLN38.desc: This is the beginning of Chapter 7 for our History of Psychology Class at UTSC (PsyC85).  This lecture focuses on Sigmund Freud

mYbl8Gx7rBM.title: Module 5B - Anna Freud, Alfred Adler & Karen Horney
mYbl8Gx7rBM.desc: Continuing on through Chapter 7, this video focuses on some of the twists others have added to Freud's general theory, including those by his daughter Anna.  It is the second of three videos for this chapter.

vatCJ9Wr2h8.title: Module 5C - Carl Jung
vatCJ9Wr2h8.desc: This one takes us to the end of Chapter 7 and focuses exclusively on Carl Jung.

rvD5v2-8sPY.title: Module 6A - Functionalism as a reaction to structuralism
rvD5v2-8sPY.desc: This video begins Chapter 8.  You will learn a lot about Titchener and his clear definition of what he thought psychology was about. 9G1NGtSvuuk.title: Module 6B - Intelligence
9G1NGtSvuuk.desc: Lecture 2 on Chapter 8, this one focuses on early attempts to define and quantify intelligence.  It features such people as Cattell, Binet and Lewis Terman

Ou58TG-gcFw.title: Module 6C - Takin Care of Business
Ou58TG-gcFw.desc: The 3rd video (of 4) for Chapter 8, this one focuses on those who brought psychology into the world of business ... including Taylor and Mayo. This is the birth of what we now call Industrial Psychology or Industrial Organization.

QlRI0ejJAts.title: Module 6D - Comparative Psychology
QlRI0ejJAts.desc: The last lecture for Chapter 8, this one focuses on the rise of comparative psychology and the influence of people like Romanes, Morgan and - of course - Edward Thorndike.  It is the period just before Behaviourism takes over psychology in America, and one can see the foundation being laid in the wo

gsS-jxMcYIk.title: Module 6E - The Russians
gsS-jxMcYIk.desc: We're now beginning Chapter 9 of our textbook.  This lecture will focus on Pavlov and Bechterev and how the set the stage for behaviourism in the United States

0nJboe3G7pQ.title: Module 6F - Watson and Lashley
0nJboe3G7pQ.desc: John B Watson, Father of Behaviourism, now makes his appearance!  Inspired by the work of Pavlov, he redefined the study of psychology, at least "As the Behaviourist Views It"

BwHGHJODt5g.title: Module 6G - Skinner
BwHGHJODt5g.desc: We're now at the end of Chapter 9 and will focus here on the work of B. F. Skinner, the radical behaviourist!

R2qCn6WgbH0.title: Module 6G - Skinner
R2qCn6WgbH0.desc: This is the end of the Behaviourism chapter wherein we encounter the radical behaviourist himself, one B. F. Skinner

3i4zwFgykRs.title: Module 7A - Wertheimer and Gestalt Psychology
3i4zwFgykRs.desc: We're starting Chapter 10 here, and suddenly a reductionist view of mental processing will be under attack!  First from the Gestalt Psychologists but soon their way of thinking will give rise to Social Psychology.  This video will focus on the first Gestalt Psychologist, Max Wetheimer

-DzQaxv2IFE.title: Module 7B - Köhlers, Koffka and Lewin
-DzQaxv2IFE.desc: This is the middle part of Chapter 10, where we move from class Gestalt Psychology through to some extensions of the basic "whole system" or "holistic processing" idea that will - in our next lecture - bring us to Social Psychology proper.

BFCnTiysKcw.title: Module 7C - Social Psychology is Born
BFCnTiysKcw.desc: This video covers the last part of Chapter 10 and focuses squarely on the first experiments in the field of social psychology, experiments that are now widely known and covered in virtually every Introduction to Psychology textbook.

1-9T3Dm4Dgc.title: Module 7D - Research Methods: Experimental
1-9T3Dm4Dgc.desc: Now we're into the beginning of Chapter 11.  In this chapter we'll discuss how research methods became more formalized in the 1920 - 193X era thanks largely to the work of the Vienna Circle.  This lecture will focus on the formalization of experimental methods

7JgsMCJf73k.title: Module 7E - Research Methods: Correlational
7JgsMCJf73k.desc: This covers the end of Chapter 11, focusing on correlation and factor analysis, its creation, and some of the ways it has been used,

M6jPSh8KF3E.title: Module 8A - Hilgard, Guthrie, Hull and Tolman
M6jPSh8KF3E.desc: Welcome to Chapter 12, a world after behaviourism but before the Cognitive Revolution.  This is a time of learning theorists, researchers who began thinking about "intervening variables" ... things related to learning the occurred between the stimulus and the response.  In this lecture we meet four

sreTOCu0GnQ.title: Module 8B - Verbal Learning
sreTOCu0GnQ.desc: Midway through Chapter 12 we learn about the verbal learning tradition that was a big part of informing learning theories, and also contributed many tasks and experimental traditions that continue to be commonly used in modern psychology experiments.  This video focuses on that work.

sKo0U_hTOns.title: Module 8C - Hebb, Sperry and Bandura
sKo0U_hTOns.desc: This is the third and last video for Chapter 12 - Learning Theories.  This one actually highlights two different approaches to understanding learning, one the focuses on a brain-based perspective (Hebb & Sperry) and another that focuses on the importance of social influences on learning (Bandura).

lvLnOSrN5-U.title: Second peerScholar activity
lvLnOSrN5-U.desc: In this video I describe the second peerScholar activity for our PsyC85 History of Psychology course.  Simulating conversations between famous psychologists!

gPY0SJdIHjM.title: Module 9B - Piaget & Vygotsky
gPY0SJdIHjM.desc: The second of three lectures from Chapter 13, this one focuses on two of the giants of development psychology and educational psychology; Jean Piaget and Lev Vygotsky.

rcrgh69Z0mI.title: Module 9C - Erikson & E. Gibson
rcrgh69Z0mI.desc: This is the last lecture related to Chapter 13 - Developmental Psychology.  In this one we discuss the work of Erik Erikson and Eleanor Gibson

efeC7m0D3Ms.title: Module 10A - Existential Philosophy
efeC7m0D3Ms.desc: If you have not encountered existential philosophy before, prepare to have your mind messed with!  This is the beginning of Chapter 14 and it sets the stage for some of the Humanistic approaches to psychology we will discuss next.

kDTQir5kR1c.title: Module 10B - May and Maslow
kDTQir5kR1c.desc: Now that you have a sense of existential philosophy, we'll discuss how Humanistic Psychology emerged and was situated within existentialism. PjQAwAdabJE.title: Module 10C - Rogers, Gendlin and Kelly
PjQAwAdabJE.desc: This video covers the end of Chapter 14 and focused on the humanistic approach to therapy and well being in general.  We'll discuss the work and ideas of Rogers, Gendlin and Kelly.

fNNZWknIA6g.title: Module 11A - Chomsky, Miller, Bruner & Bartlett
fNNZWknIA6g.desc: This begins Chapter 15, our second last chapter. ATTC2yR96BQ.title: Module 11B - Neisser, Gibson, Simon and the Role of Computers
ATTC2yR96BQ.desc: This lecture covers the end of Chapter 15, and really lays out the early days of Cognitive Psychology.  I emphasize how important computers have been, first in providing an analogy to human information processing, but later becoming tools for computational theories of mind.

-xJANNMH8pA.title: Module 11C - The Future of the History of Psychology
-xJANNMH8pA.desc:

wRAc3QQlWdQ.title: [PSYC200] 15. Consciousness Part 1: Variations and Rhythms
wRAc3QQlWdQ.desc:

Ex7xXQ6shfk.title: [PSYC200] 16. Consciousness Part 2: Sleep Stages and Deprivation

0qhxGGVehuw.title: [PSYC200] 18. Learning: Classical Conditioning

-8OGoStniYU.desc:
